items.title: Approval and Adoption of Minutes
Approval and Adoption of Minutes
Opening Remarks
Mayor Shawn Watters welcomed everyone to their first budget
notes: discussion following the election.

items.title: Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer gave a presentation providing
notes: an executive summary of the 2023 budget and outlined the budget process. He indicated there are many competing priorities for funding including growth and maintaining service levels in a high inflation environment.

He indicated staff are presenting a Township Levy increase of 3.48% representing a $45 increase to taxes on the average property assessed at $384,898. This results in a blended rate of 3.19% which includes County, Township and the Education levy. He further reviewed the sources of funding in the operating budget.
7. 2023 Draft Budget
7.1 Budget Presentation

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer reviewed the Asset Management planning process, the link to the annual budget process and the planning recommendations from the Asset Management Plan, the public engagement process to the 2023 budget and the 2023 Fees and Charges By-law.

Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer reviewed the Tax supported operating budget explaining the average residential Tax Bill breakdown, how the municipal budget works, shared budget facts indicating the Township operating budget is $49.3 million dollars and reviewed the budget timeline. He outlined the current funding challenges, highlighted areas with a dollar impact of over $10 000 and how the Township is paying for growth.
M. Bradey further reviewed the 2023 Capital Budget sources of funding.
A. McNabb reviewed the debt analysis from 2022 through to 2033.
7.2 Staffing Strategy

D. Wilson gave a presentation on the staffing strategy. He outlined the reasons for proposed staff positions, the purpose and guiding principles of the strategy and the staff forecast from 2023 through 2025.
Staff responded to questions regarding administrative support in the CAO’s office, legislated QMS positions, Climate Change Coordinator and Manager of Planning.
Council recessed at 10:48 am and resumed 11:01 am.
7.3 2023 Operating Budget
Deputy Mayor Jefferson called the meeting back to order.
M. Bradey reviewed the 2023 tax supported operating budget summary by division.

Staff outlined the process to handle proposed Council changes to the budget and responded to questions regarding staffing, ownership and use of 205 Queen Street, cyber security protection, conference and training expenses, animal control, and garbage pick up in the downtown core.
Council recessed from 12:17pm and resumed at 12:50pm.

M. Bradey continued with the review of the tax supported operating budget by division and responded to questions regarding crossing guard recruitment, recreation programming, renovations to the Elora Community Centre and Belwood Hall, public tree permits, downtown beatification including Belwood, community impact grants and neighbourhood grants.
Council recessed recess from 2:04pm and resumed 2:14pm
M. Bradey continued with the review of the tax supported operating budget.
Staff responded to questions regarding the GRCA levy, health care recruitment, and the LCBO rental agreement.
Deputy Mayor Jefferson having declared a conflict of interest left the room while staff reviewed the Fergus BIA levy.
Mayor Watters assumed the Chair.
M. Bradey continued review of the operating budget with the Elora BIA budget.
Staff responded to further questions regarding tax increment equivalent grant expenses and the dedicated capital levy.
M. Bradey explained the draft 3-year operating forecast summary and indicated it is for Council information and reviewed the water and wastewater operating budget.
M. Bradey reviewed the draft Capital Budget, explained how the capital budget is formulated and staff answered questions regarding traffic calming, road conditions and speed limit studies.
Staff responded to further questions for clarification regarding the capital budget as well as including low emissions vehicles to the fleet, and the Middlebrook bridge project.
Deputy Mayor Jefferson reviewed the current parking lot items.

Mayor Watter requested short term rental / business licence review study, Councillor Lustgarten-Evoy and Adams requested staffing in the CAO office, Councillor Adams requested an increase in the contribution to the capital budget, and Councillor Wilton requested an increase to the traffic calming measures.
would return at 5:00pm for the delegations.

items.title: Delegations - 5:00 PM
John Scott, Green Lanes Centre Wellington requested streets be
notes: designed for more than just one mode of transportation and an increase in funding to the traffic calming budget. He shared statistics and facts about multi vehicle street design and shared stories about people who are unable to drive anymore and how they get around.

items.title: Dr. Sarah Gower addressed Council regarding Health Care Recruitment
notes: Funding. She outlined the current issue in the health care system and the introduction of the use of hospitalist positions where physicians assist at Groves Memorial to assess hospital patients and the addition of temporary emergency staff from out of town requiring temporary housing while working in Centre Wellington.
Councillor MacDonald requested clarification on what would be the most beneficial for assistance to the hospital.
Councillor Lustgarten-Evoy requested clarification if they are looking for additional funding to the $20 000 and asked for further explanation on what funding is required for.

items.title: Deputy Mayor Jefferson having declared a conflict left the room. Mayor
notes: Watters assumed the Chair.

Talia Jenkins, Chair of the Board, Fergus BIA informed Council of the new executive and reviewed the membership. She reviewed the events and challenges of 2022 including garbage collection and indicated they requesting a 6% increase which amounts to approximately $3000 to the levy.

items.title: Deputy Mayor Jefferson returned to the meeting and reassumed the
notes: Chair.

Maclean Hann, Chair of the Board, Elora BIA reviewed the composition of the executive board and the successes of 2022. He indicated they are requesting a 7% levy increase to assist in hosting additional events.

items.title: Randy Vaine, resident withdrew his delegation request.
Stephen Kitras addressed Council asking for the creation of a public
notes: advisory finance committee and reviewed the qualifications of the individuals he felt should form the advisory committee.

He indicated Council could control costs by controlling staffing and the use of the building reserve to cover part of the staffing cost as well as only adding positions that are legally required. Further, he would like Council to reconsider the development of the operations facility and consider funding attainable housing.

items.title: Councillor Craddock having declared a conflict left the meeting.
notes: Millicent Gordon, CW Black Community outlined the three main events hosted by the CW Black Community for black history month, including the global black mobile museum on February 16 at John Black Public School sponsored by UGDSB, and Awakened Voices February 18 and February 25. She indicated they are seeking $3000 to assist in covering the costs of the event.

13. 2023 Draft Budget Continued

13.1 M. Bradey reviewed the vehicle and equipment replacement forecast as approved at the pre budget meeting in January for 2023. He indicated the 2023 and 2024 replacement was approved in January 2023 to allow for the issuance of tenders.
Staff responded to questions regarding hybrid vehicles and rental of equipment when possible.
M. Bradey summarized the 10 year capital forecast reminding Council that years 1 through 9 are fully funded and year 10 is not fundable but all projects are kept in this year for tracking purposes.

Staff responded to questions regarding the Beatty Hollow neighbourhood park and splash pad, outdoor youth activities available in the community, renovations required at 495 Union Street, customer service and engagement strategy, council chamber technology upgrades, termite management, active transportation in rural areas and traffic calming, new wells, and accessible parks.
Staff further indicated a report regarding Urban Forestry will be provided at a future Council meeting.
M. Bradey reviewed the Reserves / Reserve Funds; he indicated the Reserve and Reserve fun policy was last updated in 2021 and noted some funds are legislated while others are Council initiated.

A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer explained when the reserve and reserve fund policy is brought forward to Council for review would be the appropriate time to edit the reserves.
Staff responded to questions regarding the Wind Turbine Capital Reserve, the MacDonald Trust Fund, and the Development Charges Reserve Fund including the effects of Bill 23.
M. Bradey review the current and projected debt capacity and where new debt may be incurred.
Council recessed at 10:37am and returned at 10:55am.
